## Equations of Motion

The system is a symmetric rigid body ($I_1=I_2$) with Euler angles $(\theta,\varphi,\psi)$ (standard convention: $\theta$ = nutation between body symmetry axis $\mathbf e_3$ and the space-fixed vertical $\mathbf e_z$, $\varphi$ = precession about $\mathbf e_z$, $\psi$ = spin about $\mathbf e_3$).

**Kinetic energy** (body-frame angular velocity $\omega_3=\dot\psi+\dot\varphi\cos\theta$):
$$T=\tfrac12 I_1\bigl(\dot\theta^{\,2}+\dot\varphi^{\,2}\sin^2\theta\bigr)+\tfrac12 I_3(\dot\psi+\dot\varphi\cos\theta)^2.$$

**Potential energy** (given):
$$U=-\tfrac{\Omega^2}{2}(I_3-I_1)\cos^2\theta.$$

**Lagrangian** $L=T-U$. Since $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are cyclic, the Euler–Lagrange equations are:

1. **$\psi$-equation** (spin about symmetry axis):
$$I_3(\dot\psi+\dot\varphi\cos\theta)=L_3=\text{const},$$
where $L_3$ is the angular momentum about the body symmetry axis.

2. **$\varphi$-equation** (precession):
$$I_1\dot\varphi\sin^2\theta+L_3\cos\theta=L_z=\text{const},$$
where $L_z$ is the angular momentum about the space vertical.

3. **$\theta$-equation** (nutation):
$$I_1\ddot\theta=I_1\dot\varphi^{\,2}\sin\theta\cos\theta-L_3\dot\varphi\sin\theta-\Omega^2(I_3-I_1)\sin\theta\cos\theta.$$

**Energy** is also conserved:
$$E=\tfrac12 I_1\dot\theta^{\,2}+\frac{(L_z-L_3\cos\theta)^2}{2I_1\sin^2\theta}+\frac{L_3^2}{2I_3}-\tfrac{\Omega^2}{2}(I_3-I_1)\cos^2\theta.$$

Eliminating $\dot\varphi=(L_z-L_3\cos\theta)/(I_1\sin^2\theta)$ gives the reduced one-degree-of-freedom problem
$$\tfrac12 I_1\dot\theta^{\,2}+V_{\text{eff}}(\theta)=E,\qquad V_{\text{eff}}(\theta)=\frac{(L_z-L_3\cos\theta)^2}{2I_1\sin^2\theta}-\tfrac{\Omega^2}{2}(I_3-I_1)\cos^2\theta,$$
(up to the constant $L_3^2/(2I_3)$). The $\theta$-dynamics is governed by $I_1\ddot\theta=-V_{\text{eff}}'(\theta)$.

## Equilibrium Points

Equilibria require $\dot\theta=0$ and $\ddot\theta=0$, i.e. critical points of $V_{\text{eff}}$ with $\dot\theta=0$ (so $\dot\varphi,\dot\psi$ stay constant). Setting $V_{\text{eff}}'(\theta)=0$ with $c=\cos\theta$, $s=\sin\theta$, $A=L_z-L_3 c$:
$$\frac{A\,L_3\,s^{2}-A^{2}c}{I_1 s^{3}}+\Omega^{2}(I_3-I_1)\,c\,s=0,$$
or equivalently
$$A\,L_3\,s^{2}-A^{2}c+\Omega^{2}(I_3-I_1)I_1\,c\,s^{4}=0.\tag{$\star$}$$

The **principal (geometric) equilibrium configurations**, obtained as special solutions of $(\star)$, are:

| Equilibrium | Condition | Physical meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta=0$ | $L_z=L_3$ | Symmetry axis $\mathbf e_3$ aligned with space vertical $\mathbf e_z$ (upright spin); $U=-\tfrac{\Omega^2}{2}(I_3-I_1)$, the **minimum** of $U$. |
| $\theta=\pi$ | $L_z=-L_3$ | Symmetry axis anti-aligned with $\mathbf e_z$ (inverted spin); same energy, also a **minimum** of $U$. |
| $\theta=\pi/2$ | $L_z\,L_3=0$ | Symmetry axis perpendicular to $\mathbf e_z$ (horizontal); $U=0$, a **maximum** of $U$. Stable only with suitable angular momentum ($L_z=0$ or $L_3=0$). |

The **general family** of equilibria is the one-parameter set (parametrized by the constants $L_z,L_3$) of $\theta\in(0,\pi)$ satisfying $(\star)$, with the corresponding constant rates
$$\dot\varphi=\frac{L_z-L_3\cos\theta}{I_1\sin^2\theta},\qquad \dot\psi=\frac{L_3}{I_3}-\dot\varphi\cos\theta.$$

**Stability remark.** Since $U=-\tfrac{\Omega^2}{2}(I_3-I_1)\cos^2\theta$ and for Earth $I_3>I_1$ (oblate), $U$ is minimized at $\theta=0,\pi$ and maximized at $\theta=\pi/2$. Hence the upright/inverted configurations $\theta=0,\pi$ are energetically favored (stable for small $L_3,L_z$), while $\theta=\pi/2$ is a saddle/maximum of the potential and is generically unstable, becoming an equilibrium only under the fine-tuned condition $L_zL_3=0$.

## Equations of Motion

The system is a symmetric rigid body ($I_1=I_2$) with Euler angles $(\theta,\varphi,\psi)$ (standard convention: $\theta$ = nutation between body symmetry axis $\mathbf e_3$ and the space-fixed vertical $\mathbf e_z$, $\varphi$ = precession about $\mathbf e_z$, $\psi$ = spin about $\mathbf e_3$).

**Kinetic energy** (body-frame angular velocity $\omega_3=\dot\psi+\dot\varphi\cos\theta$):
$$T=\tfrac12 I_1\bigl(\dot\theta^{\,2}+\dot\varphi^{\,2}\sin^2\theta\bigr)+\tfrac12 I_3(\dot\psi+\dot\varphi\cos\theta)^2.$$

**Potential energy** (given):
$$U=-\tfrac{\Omega^2}{2}(I_3-I_1)\cos^2\theta.$$

**Lagrangian** $L=T-U$. Since $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are cyclic, the Euler–Lagrange equations are:

1. **$\psi$-equation** (spin about symmetry axis):
$$I_3(\dot\psi+\dot\varphi\cos\theta)=L_3=\text{const},$$
where $L_3$ is the angular momentum about the body symmetry axis.

2. **$\varphi$-equation** (precession):
$$I_1\dot\varphi\sin^2\theta+L_3\cos\theta=L_z=\text{const},$$
where $L_z$ is the angular momentum about the space vertical.

3. **$\theta$-equation** (nutation):
$$I_1\ddot\theta=I_1\dot\varphi^{\,2}\sin\theta\cos\theta-L_3\dot\varphi\sin\theta-\Omega^2(I_3-I_1)\sin\theta\cos\theta.$$

**Energy** is also conserved:
$$E=\tfrac12 I_1\dot\theta^{\,2}+\frac{(L_z-L_3\cos\theta)^2}{2I_1\sin^2\theta}+\frac{L_3^2}{2I_3}-\tfrac{\Omega^2}{2}(I_3-I_1)\cos^2\theta.$$

Eliminating $\dot\varphi=(L_z-L_3\cos\theta)/(I_1\sin^2\theta)$ gives the reduced one-degree-of-freedom problem
$$\tfrac12 I_1\dot\theta^{\,2}+V_{\text{eff}}(\theta)=E,\qquad V_{\text{eff}}(\theta)=\frac{(L_z-L_3\cos\theta)^2}{2I_1\sin^2\theta}-\tfrac{\Omega^2}{2}(I_3-I_1)\cos^2\theta,$$
(up to the constant $L_3^2/(2I_3)$). The $\theta$-dynamics is governed by $I_1\ddot\theta=-V_{\text{eff}}'(\theta)$.

## Equilibrium Points

Equilibria require $\dot\theta=0$ and $\ddot\theta=0$, i.e. critical points of $V_{\text{eff}}$ with $\dot\theta=0$ (so $\dot\varphi,\dot\psi$ stay constant). Setting $V_{\text{eff}}'(\theta)=0$ with $c=\cos\theta$, $s=\sin\theta$, $A=L_z-L_3 c$:
$$\frac{A\,L_3\,s^{2}-A^{2}c}{I_1 s^{3}}+\Omega^{2}(I_3-I_1)\,c\,s=0,$$
or equivalently
$$A\,L_3\,s^{2}-A^{2}c+\Omega^{2}(I_3-I_1)I_1\,c\,s^{4}=0.\tag{$\star$}$$

The **principal (geometric) equilibrium configurations**, obtained as special solutions of $(\star)$, are:

| Equilibrium | Condition | Physical meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta=0$ | $L_z=L_3$ | Symmetry axis $\mathbf e_3$ aligned with space vertical $\mathbf e_z$ (upright spin); $U=-\tfrac{\Omega^2}{2}(I_3-I_1)$, the **minimum** of $U$. |
| $\theta=\pi$ | $L_z=-L_3$ | Symmetry axis anti-aligned with $\mathbf e_z$ (inverted spin); same energy, also a **minimum** of $U$. |
| $\theta=\pi/2$ | $L_z\,L_3=0$ | Symmetry axis perpendicular to $\mathbf e_z$ (horizontal); $U=0$, a **maximum** of $U$. Stable only with suitable angular momentum ($L_z=0$ or $L_3=0$). |

The **general family** of equilibria is the one-parameter set (parametrized by the constants $L_z,L_3$) of $\theta\in(0,\pi)$ satisfying $(\star)$, with the corresponding constant rates
$$\dot\varphi=\frac{L_z-L_3\cos\theta}{I_1\sin^2\theta},\qquad \dot\psi=\frac{L_3}{I_3}-\dot\varphi\cos\theta.$$

**Stability remark.** Since $U=-\tfrac{\Omega^2}{2}(I_3-I_1)\cos^2\theta$ and for Earth $I_3>I_1$ (oblate), $U$ is minimized at $\theta=0,\pi$ and maximized at $\theta=\pi/2$. Hence the upright/inverted configurations $\theta=0,\pi$ are energetically favored (stable for small $L_3,L_z$), while $\theta=\pi/2$ is a saddle/maximum of the potential and is generically unstable, becoming an equilibrium only under the fine-tuned condition $L_zL_3=0$.
